Both landed on the same three, which is the main thing. They feel pretty different to build, though.

Version B — typing Rome and then clicking the tag chips — is the friendlier one to reach for casually. But I can see its ceiling: it's an "any of these / all of these" toggle, and that's about it. The moment I want something a little more particular, it runs out of room.

Version A, where I write out "Rome in articles or books" as a sentence, looks slightly more fussy at first, but it's the one that won't box me in. Because here's the kind of thing I know I'll eventually want: "Rome, and either articles or books, but not the ones tagged travel" — grouping a couple of tags together with an "or" and then excluding another. A typed search can carry that in one line; a row of toggle chips really can't.

So I'll go with Version A. Two things I want to confirm come with it, since they're the whole reason I'm picking it: I can single out a tag specifically (not have "books" the word accidentally match a description), and I can use "and," "or," "not," and group things in parentheses. Does A handle an exclude like "not travel" and a grouped "(articles or books)" too?
